Drug Testing Statistics in the USA



Drug testing in the US workforce has seen fluctuations in positivity rates and drug-specific trends in recent years.  Here is a look at some keys statistics:


Overall drug test positivity
Historically High Rates: Overall drug positivity in the general US workforce has remained at historically high levels, with rates around 4.6% in 2021 and 2022, and 5.7% in both 2022 and 2023. This is the highest level in over two decades, up significantly from lows of 3.5% in 2010-2012. Tampering on the Rise: The percentage of employees attempting to subvert the drug testing process through tampering with specimens (substituted or invalid samples) has surged. Substituted urine specimens increased by over 600% in 2023 compared to the prior year, reaching the highest rate ever reported. Invalid urine specimens also increased by 45.2%.

Marijuana Use
Continued Upward Trend: Marijuana positivity rates have consistently climbed, reaching their highest levels ever recorded in both the general workforce and post-accident tests. Impact of Legalization: In states where recreational marijuana is legal, the positivity rate for marijuana in the general workforce was significantly higher (5.7% in 2022) than the national average (4.3% in 2022). However, marijuana positivity decreased in the federally mandated, safety-sensitive workforce, potentially due to the deterrent effect of expected drug testing in those roles. Post-Accident Positivity Soars: Post-accident marijuana positivity in the general workforce reached a 25-year high in 2022 and continues to climb, showing a 114.3% increase between 2015 and 2023.


Other Drugs
Amphetamines: Positivity for amphetamines has shown an upward trend, increasing by a fifth of a percentage point from 2021 to 2022, particularly among employees in the Education Services industry. Note that testing does not distinguish between legally prescribed and illicit use. Opiates: Overall positivity for opiates (codeine/morphine) in the general workforce has decreased over the last five years. Heroin and other opiates also showed decreases in positivity rates. Cocaine: Cocaine positivity in the general workforce showed a slight increase in 2022 but has declined over the past five years.

Workplace Drug Testing Landscape
Commonality: Roughly 63% of organizations conduct some form of alcohol or drug testing, a figure that has remained relatively stable over the years. Testing Methods: Urine tests are the most common, used by about 85% of companies, followed by saliva and hair tests. Industry Variation: The prevalence of drug testing varies across industries. Government positions, healthcare, and transportation are among the most likely to require drug tests. Note: These statistics primarily focus on workplace drug testing and may not fully represent drug use across the general population. Data collection and reporting methods may also vary between organizations.

Commonly used for pre-employment, random, post-accident, court-ordered, and DOT-regulated testing, urine drug screens provide reliable results within 1-3 days.

  • Marijuana

  • Opiates (morphine, codeine heroin)

Urine Drug Testing Overview

Alcohol Testing Near Me

Alcohol testing, also commonly referred to as alcohol drug testing, is a process used to detect the presence and concentration of alcohol (ethanol) in a person\'s system. Unlike standard drug tests, which typically identify substance use over several days or weeks, alcohol testing is specifically designed to detect recent consumption, often within the past few hours.

Order Your Test Online

Common Alcohol Testing Methods

Our Alcohol Testing Locations Near You provide

  • Breath Alcohol Testing (BAT)
  • Urine Alcohol Testing
  • Blood Alcohol Testing
  • Hair Follicle Alcohol Testing
  • Oral Fluid Alcohol Testing

Why Is Alcohol Testing Important?

  • To enforce workplace safety and zero tolerance policies
  • Compliance with DO Regulations (49 CFR Part 40)
  • Post accident/reasonable Suspicion testing
  • Probation, court ordered or child custody cases
  • Alcohol recovery monitoring

Breath Alcohol Tests: Breath alcohol tests are the most commonly used method for the immediate detection of alcohol in a person\'s system. Utilizing breathalyzers, this test measures Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) through exhaled breath. Results are available within minutes and are frequently used in roadside law enforcement, workplace screenings, and DOT-regulated testing programs. Certified Breath Alcohol Technicians (BATs) must administer these tests in compliance with federal guidelines.

Urine Alcohol Test Urine testing can detect both recent and extended alcohol use depending on the type of analysis: Standard Urine Alcohol Test: Detects the presence of ethanol and is typically effective for up to 8-12 hours after consumption. A more complex Ethyl Glucuronide (ETG) and Ethyl Sulfate (ETS) metabolites of alcohol which can detect alcohol consumption up to 80 hours. These metabolite-based tests can detect alcohol consumption for up to 80 hours, even after the ethanol has body. This is often used in abstinence monitoring, court-ordered testing, and alcohol treatmnet programs. Saliva (oral fluid) Alcohol Testing: Saliva testing is a fast, non-invasive method that detects alcohol use within 12 to 24 hours. It is ideal for post-incident or reasonable suspicion testing and is easy to administer in both clinical and field settings. Oral fluid tests can be used for both screening and confirmation, offering a convenient alternative to breath or urine testing.
Blood Alcohol Testing:Blood tests offer the most precise measurement of a person\'s current BAC and are often used in medical, legal, or forensic contexts. Although more invasive and costly than other methods, blood alcohol tests provide a reliable, real-time snapshot of impairment at the moment the sample is collected. This method is often used following serious accidents or in DUI investigations.
Hair Follicle Alcohol Test:Hair testing is designed to detect long-term, chronic alcohol consumption. It identifies alcohol biomarkers such as Fatty Acid Ethyl Esters (FAEEs) and Ethyl Glucuronide (ETG).These biomarkers can remain in hair for up to 90 days, providing a historical profile of alcohol use. Hair alcohol testing is commonly used in family court cases, custody evaluations, and addiction recovery programs to demonstrate patterns of excessive or repeated alcohol use over time.

Hair Follicle Drug Testing Near Me

Hair follicle drug testing also commonly referred to as hair drug testing, is a highly accurate and reliable method used to detect patterns of long-term drug use. This testing method analyzes a small sample of hair to identify the presence of drugs and their metabolites, which are deposited in the hair shaft via the bloodstream following drug consumption. Unlike urine or oral fluid tests that detect recent use, hair drug tests provide a significantly longer detection window of  up to 90 days, making them ideal for identifying chronic or repeated drug use over time.

Order Your Test Online

How Does Hair Testing Work?

  • A sample of approximately 1.5 inches of hair is collected, typically from the crown of the scalp.
  • Because human hair grows at an average rate of an 1/2 inch per month, a 1.5-inch sample can detect drug use over the past 90 days.
  • If no head hair is available, body hair options are available
  • Certified Labs use a two-step testing process
  • 1. Initial ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) screening
  • 2. Confirmatory GC/MS or LC/MS/MS (Gas or Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry)

What Substances Can Hair Follicle Drug Tests Detect?

  • Amphetamines (including methamphetamine and ecstasy)
  • Cocaine
  • Opiates (heroin, morphine, codeine)
  • Phencyclidine (PCP)
  • Benzodiazepines
  • Synthetic opioids (fentanyl, oxycodone)

    What to Expect When You Arrive at a Drug Testing Location Near You?

    Whether you\'re completing a drug test for employment, DOT compliance, court-ordered testing, or another reason, understanding the process can help ensure a smooth and stress-free experience. Here\'s what you can expect when arriving at a collection site for drug testing:

    1. Arrival and Check-in
    Please ensure you bring  a valid government issued photo ID such as a drivers license a or passport and your donor registration form, which is emailed to you upon registration. To help expedite the process please arrive ready to use the restroom or provide a sample.

    2. Test Procedure
    The testing process will depend on the type of test ordered, listed below are the two most common types of samples outlined:

    Urine Drug Testing Near You

    • Be prepared to empty your pockets and store belongings
    • Wash your hands
    • Collector will provide or you may select a sealed collection cup and proceed to the restroom to provide a sample

    Hair Drug Testing Near You
    • Be prepared to empty your pockets and store belongings

    • Standard Hair collection (90 days) will require approximately 100-120 strands cut from the crown of the head
    • If no head hair is available, a body hair sample may be collected (cotton ball size)
    • Complete and required Chain of custody paperwork

    3. Chain of Custody
    • All certified labs require a chain of custody form (CCF) to be completed by the collector and the donor. This provides proper documentation for the lab, ensures specimen tracking and tamper proof handling
    • The collector will complete the CCF and the donor will sign the CCF to confirm the specimen was collected belongs to the donor
    • Collector will place the specimen and chain of custody in the tamper evident bag in the donor\'s presence and secure it until shipment
    • Sealed specimen is shipped via courier to the laboratory for analysis

    4. Test Completion
    • Most specimen collections typically take 15-30 minutes
    • Upon completion, the donor will receive a copy of the CCF as proof you have taken your test
    • You do not receive your test results at the collection facility, once analyzed they will be sent to the Medical Review Officer (MRO) and released via email to the email address provided during the test registration process

    5. After the Test
    • Urine results take approximately 24-48 hours from the time the specimen arrives at the lab.
    • Periodically during employment
    • After workplace injuries or incidents
    • During return-to-duty evaluations
    • As part of OSHA or DOT compliance
    6. Important Tips
    • Do not drink excessive fluids (before a urine test)
    • Arrive on time to avoid delays or rescheduling
    • Be honest and cooperative with the collector
    • Ask questions if you are unsure about any part of the process

    What Happens to a Urine Sample at a SAMHSA-Certified Laboratory

    When a urine sample is collected for drug testing, especially under Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. It is sent to a SAMHSA-certified laboratory for analysis. These labs follow strict federal protocols under 49 CFR Part 40 and HHS Mandatory Guidelines to ensure integrity, accuracy, and defensibility of the results.

    Step 1: Specimen Receipt and Accessioning

    • Chain of Custody Verification: The sealed specimen and Custody and Control Form (CCF) are verified. If there are discrepancies, the specimen may be rejected.
    • Accessioning: The sample is logged into the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) and assigned a unique accession number for tracking.

    Step 2: Initial Screening (Immunoassay)

    The urine undergoes automated immunoassay testing to detect drug classes such as:

    • Amphetamines
    • Cocaine metabolites
    • Marijuana (THC) metabolites
    • Opiates
    • Phencyclidine (PCP)

    If no drugs or only trace levels are detected, the result is reported as Negative.

    Step 3: Confirmatory Testing (GC/MS or LC/MS/MS)

    Presumptive positives are confirmed using advanced testing methods like:

    • Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (GC/MS)
    • Liquid Chromatography/Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC/MS/MS)

    These tests provide high accuracy and confirm the specific drug and concentration.

    Step 4: Certification and Result Reporting

    • A Certifying Scientist reviews all results and documentation.
    • The final test result is certified and securely reported to the Medical Review Officer (MRO).

    Possible result categories include:

    • Negative
    • Positive (with drug type and level)
    • Rejected for testing
    • Invalid
    • Substituted
    • Adulterated
    • Dilute

    Step 5: MRO Review

    The MRO evaluates non-negative results and may contact the donor to verify any legitimate medical explanation (e.g., prescriptions). Final verified results are then issued to the employer or authorized party.

    Quality Control and Compliance

    SAMHSA-certified labs must adhere to federal standards, including:

    • Chain-of-custody procedures
    • HHS and DOT guidelines
    • Proficiency testing and quality assurance
    • Validated methods and instruments

    Summary: Urine Drug Testing Workflow

    1. Specimen received and accessioned
    2. Initial immunoassay screening
    3. Confirmation testing if needed
    4. Scientific review and certification
    5. MRO review and final result reporting

    For more information on DOT or non-DOT testing procedures, or to schedule a test, call (800) 221-4291 or visit our website.


    What Happens to a Hair Drug Testing Process at a Certified Laboratory

    Hair drug testing provides a 90-day detection window and is widely used in forensic, workplace, and court-ordered testing environments. After collection, the hair specimen is shipped to a certified laboratory for analysis using strict scientific protocols. Here\'s a detailed look at how the process works from receipt to result reporting.

    Step 1: Specimen Receipt and Chain-of-Custody Verification

    • Delivery and Inspection: The hair specimen arrives in a sealed pouch along with a Custody and Control Form (CCF).
    • Chain-of-Custody Review: The lab verifies the integrity of the seal and checks that the specimen ID matches the CCF.
    • Accessioning: The sample is logged into the laboratory system and assigned a unique accession number for tracking.

    Step 2: Hair Preparation and Decontamination

    • Cutting and Weighing: The required portion of hair (typically 3.9 cm) is separated and prepared for analysis.
    • Decontamination: The hair is washed using organic solvents and aqueous solutions to remove external contaminants.
    • Drying: The hair is dried in a controlled environment before digestion and analysis.

    Step 3: Digestion and Extraction

    • Pulverization: The hair is cut or ground into small fragments.
    • Chemical Digestion: The sample is broken down using acid or enzymes to release embedded drug metabolites.
    • Extraction: The digested solution undergoes liquid-liquid or solid-phase extraction to isolate target compounds.

    Step 4: Screening and Confirmatory Testing

    • Initial Screening: The extract is screened using enzyme immunoassay (EIA) for drug classes such as cocaine, THC, opiates, and amphetamines.
    • Confirmatory Testing: Presumptive positives are analyzed using GC/MS or LC/MS/MS to confirm the drug identity and concentration.

    Step 5: Review, Certification, and Reporting

    • Scientific Review: A certifying scientist evaluates all data, including test results, instrumentation, and chain-of-custody.
    • Result Classification: The sample is reported as Negative, Positive (with drug concentrations), Rejected, QNS (Quantity Not Sufficient), or Invalid.
    • Reporting: Results are sent to the ordering party or Medical Review Officer (MRO) for final verification and interpretation.

    Laboratory Compliance and Quality Control

    • Adherence to CAP, CLIA, or ISO/IEC 17025 standards
    • Blind proficiency testing and quality assurance protocols
    • Validated instrumentation and documentation retention

    Process Summary

    1. Specimen received and chain of custody verified
    2. Hair decontaminated and prepared
    3. Digestion and metabolite extraction
    4. Screening and GC/MS or LC/MS/MS confirmation
    5. Certification and secure result reporting

    Need to schedule a hair drug test or want to learn more? Call (800) 221-4291 or visit our website for fast, nationwide service.

The Real Cost of Drug Abuse in the Workplace

by John Burgos
on July 24, 2025
Categories: education

Why a Drug-Free Workplace Program Isn't Just Smart- It's Essential

Substance abuse doesn't just impact individuals- it significantly affects the businesses that employ them. For U.S. employers, the cost of drug and alcohol abuse is staggering, with estimates reaching $81 billion per year in lost productivity, increased healthcare expenses, absenteeism, and workplace accidents.

The Impact on Business Operations

Drug abuse in the workplace contributes to:

  • Reduced productivity and poor job performance

  • Increased absenteeism and turnover

  • Higher healthcare and workers' compensation costs

  • Safety hazards, especially in safety-sensitive industries

  • Workplace theft and liability concerns

These issues aren't rare. In fact, an estimated 70% of Americans who use illegal drugs are currently employed. Without an effective drug-free workplace program in place, companies may be unknowingly exposed to serious risks- both financial and operational.

The Numbers Speak for Themselves

$25.5 billion- Estimated cost of lost productivity and absenteeism

$25 billion- Annual healthcare costs tied to substance abuse

    $81 billion- Total annual cost of drug abuse to U.S. employers

      80% - Percentage of drug users who admit to stealing from their workplace to support their habits (NIDA, 1994)

      Why a Drug-Free Workplace Policy Matters

      Implementing a formal drug-free workplace policy is a powerful step toward protecting your team and your customers. A well-structured program includes clear guidelines, employee education, and routine or random drug testing. When employees understand expectations and consequences, they're more likely to remain accountable and safe.

      Benefits of a Drug-Free Workplace Program:

      • Fewer accidents and safety violations

      • Reduced absenteeism and turnover

      • Lower insurance and healthcare premiums

      • Better morale and team trust

      • Stronger compliance with DOT and state regulations

      Take a Proactive Approach

      Don't wait for an incident to happen. Accredited Drug Testing can help you design and implement a customized drug-free workplace program that fits your industry, workforce, and compliance requirements. From pre-employment screening to random testing and policy development, ADT is your trusted partner in promoting workplace safety and accountability.

Urine Alcohol Testing

Urine alcohol testing is a widely used method for detecting recent alcohol consumption. While alcohol is only present in urine for a short windowâ€”typically 6 to 24 hoursâ€”this testing method is useful for post-accident testing, reasonable suspicion, and compliance programs. Urine testing may also be used to detect alcohol metabolites like ETG (Ethyl Glucuronide) and ETS (Ethyl Sulfate), which significantly extend the detection period. Accredited Drug Testing offers urine alcohol testing at over 20,000 certified collection sites nationwide, ensuring rapid scheduling and accurate results.

Urine alcohol testing is one of the most widely used and cost-effective methods for detecting recent alcohol consumption in both workplace and legal settings. Blood Alcohol Testing

Blood alcohol testing is considered the most accurate method for determining Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) at the time of collection. It measures the exact amount of ethanol in the bloodstream and is commonly used in legal and medical settings, such as DUI investigations and emergency room assessments. This method requires a trained phlebotomist and is often used when precise, court-admissible results are required. Accredited Drug Testing partners with SAMHSA Certified labs to provide reliable blood alcohol testing for individuals and organizations.

  • High Accuracy and Precision One of the primary benefits of blood alcohol testing is its unmatched accuracy. It directly measures blood alcohol concentration (BAC), providing real-time insights into an individualâ€™s level of impairment.   • Legally Defensible in Court Because it offers scientifically valid results, blood alcohol testing is widely accepted in court proceedings, including DUI cases, workplace litigation, and civil matters. Results from a certified laboratory can be presented as admissible evidence when collected and handled properly with a documented chain of custody
  • Real-Time Impairment Detection Unlike urine or hair tests, blood alcohol testing shows current levels of alcohol in the system, making it ideal for determining whether someone was impaired at the time of an incident. This is especially important in DUI cases or after a workplace accident where impairment may be a contributing factor.
  • Supports Medical Diagnoses and Emergency Response Hospitals and emergency rooms often rely on blood alcohol tests to assess intoxication levels, guide treatment decisions, and rule out alcohol-related conditions. Medical professionals trust this method due to its clinical accuracy and quick turnaround times
  • Tamper-Resistant and Secure Blood tests are collected by licensed medical personnel and analyzed in CLIA-certified laboratories, making them highly secure and resistant to adulteration. This adds a layer of credibility and trust in high-stakes environments like law enforcement or federal compliance programs.

Breath Alcohol Testing

Breath alcohol testing (BAT) is a fast, non-invasive method approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for workplace drug and alcohol testing programs. It detects current impairment by measuring alcohol content in deep-lung breath using an Evidential Breath Testing (EBT) device. Results are available instantly and are legally defensible when conducted by a certified breath alcohol technician (BAT). Accredited Drug Testing offers DOT-compliant breath alcohol tests for random, post-accident, and reasonable suspicion testing.

Order Your Test Online

Breath alcohol testingâ€”commonly referred to as a breathalyzer testâ€”is one of the most efficient, non-invasive, and immediate methods for detecting alcohol impairment. Widely used in both law enforcement and workplace safety programs, this method measures Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) through a breath sample using an Evidential Breath Testing (EBT) device. At Accredited Drug Testing, we offer DOT-compliant breath alcohol testing services nationwide, ensuring fast, legally defensible results for employers, courts, and individuals


    Key Benefits of Breath Alcohol Testing

  • Instant, Legally Admissible Results Breath alcohol testing provides real-time results in minutes, making it ideal for situations where immediate decision-making is criticalâ€”such as post-accident or reasonable suspicion testing. When performed using a DOT-approved EBT device, results are admissible in court and compliant with federal regulations.
  • Non-Invasive and Hassle-Free Unlike blood or urine tests, a breath alcohol test is completely non-invasiveâ€”requiring no bodily fluids or medical personnel. This makes it ideal for on-site workplace testing, roadside checks, and high-throughput testing events.
  • DOT-Approved and Federally Compliant Breath alcohol testing is the primary method authorized by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for alcohol screening under 49 CFR Part 40. It is required for safety-sensitive employees in industries such as trucking, aviation, pipeline, rail, and transit, making it an essential tool for compliance.
  • Effective Impairment Detection Breath testing measures current alcohol levels, unlike ETG or hair tests that identify past use. This makes breath alcohol testing ideal for determining real-time impairment in safety-sensitive roles or during active investigations.
  • Highly Accessible and Scalable Breath alcohol testing can be conducted virtually anywhere with a portable EBT deviceâ€”no lab processing required. Accredited Drug Testing offers mobile testing units and on-site breath alcohol testing for companies that need large-scale or remote solutions.
  • . Reduces Risk and Liability Implementing a breath alcohol testing program helps employers mitigate liability, promote a safe work environment, and comply with federal regulations. Routine screening can prevent accidents, reduce workersâ€™ comp claims, and demonstrate a proactive safety culture./li>

Our certified breath alcohol technicians (BATs) and EBT devices meet all federal standards, ensuring accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance. âœ… Schedule Your Breath Alcohol Test Today â€“ Click Here to Register or call (800) 221-4291.

Hair Alcohol Testing

Hair alcohol testing is an advanced method designed to detect chronic, long-term alcohol consumption over a 90-day window. Unlike other testing methods that detect recent use, hair testing identifies alcohol markers such as ethyl glucuronide (ETG) and fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEEs) embedded in the hair shaft. It is frequently used in family court cases, substance abuse programs, and workplace compliance checks. Accredited Drug Testing offers hair alcohol testing through leading laboratories to provide accurate, tamper-resistant results.

Order Your Test Online

Hair alcohol testing is a powerful tool used to detect long-term alcohol consumption by analyzing biomarkers such as ethyl glucuronide (ETG) and fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEEs) embedded in the hair shaft. Unlike breath, blood, or urine tests, which detect recent use, hair testing provides a comprehensive 90-day look-back window, making it ideal for legal, forensic, and clinical settings. At Accredited Drug Testing, we offer certified hair alcohol testing services for employers, courts, and individuals who need a reliable method to monitor chronic alcohol use.

Key Benefits of Hair Alcohol Testing

  • Extended Detection Window â€“ Up to 90 Days One of the greatest benefits of hair alcohol testing is its ability to detect chronic alcohol consumption over a 3-month period. This makes it particularly useful for family court cases, child custody disputes, probation compliance, and treatment monitoring programs where identifying patterns of abuse is more important than identifying recent use.
  • Highly Reliable and Tamper-Resistant Because alcohol metabolites are trapped in the hair as it grows, this testing method is nearly impossible to adulterate. Hair testing is observed, non-invasive, and analyzed in SAMHSA or ISO-accredited laboratories, making it a trusted option in both legal and clinical environments.
  • Court-Admissible and Forensically Sound Hair alcohol test results are commonly accepted in civil court proceedings, particularly in cases involving custody, divorce, adoption, or immigration. The use of FAEE and ETG testing in hair is backed by extensive scientific research, making it a legally defensible option when administered by certified professionals
  • No Need for Recent Consumption Unlike breath or urine tests that require recent drinking to trigger a result, hair alcohol testing identifies repeated and excessive drinking behavior over time. This allows courts and treatment providers to assess long-term behavioral patterns, even if the individual is currently abstinent.
  • Ideal for Zero-Tolerance and Monitoring Programs Hair testing is a preferred method in zero-tolerance environments, including child welfare agencies, rehab facilities, and occupational health programs, where continuous abstinence must be verified over extended periods.

Saliva Alcohol Testing

Saliva alcohol testing, also known as oral fluid alcohol testing, is a convenient and non-invasive option that detects alcohol use within the past few hours. This method is ideal for on-site testing, roadside checks, and safety-sensitive workplaces where rapid results are needed. Saliva testing typically reflects current blood alcohol levels and can be administered without the need for specialized collection facilities. Accredited Drug Testing provides mobile and lab-based saliva alcohol testing for employers and individuals alike.

Order Your Test Online

Saliva alcohol testing, also known as oral fluid alcohol testing, is a fast, non-invasive, and cost-effective method for detecting recent alcohol use. With immediate results and simple administration, this testing method is ideal for workplace testing, law enforcement, rehabilitation programs, and personal use. At Accredited Drug Testing, we offer saliva alcohol testing services nationwide, available on-site, in-clinic, or through mobile collection units.

Key Benefits of Saliva Alcohol Testing

  • Fast and Immediate Results- Saliva alcohol tests provide real-time resultsâ€”usually within minutesâ€”making them perfect for post-accident, reasonable suspicion, and random testing scenarios where time is critical. Employers and law enforcement professionals rely on this method to make immediate safety decisions
  • Non-Invasive and Easy to Collect- Unlike blood or urine tests, oral fluid alcohol testing is non-invasive and hygienic. It requires only a quick mouth swab, with no privacy concerns or need for specialized collection environments. This makes it ideal for on-site workplace testing, remote locations, or field sobriety screenings.
  • Accurate Detection of Recent Use- Saliva testing detects the presence of alcohol consumed within the past 6 to 12 hours, making it one of the best tools for identifying active impairment. It closely reflects Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) levels and is effective for determining whether someone is under the influence at the time of testing.
  • DOT-Compatible with EBT Devices- When administered using a DOT-approved Evidential Breath Testing (EBT) device, saliva alcohol testing can be used for Department of Transportation (DOT) compliance under 49 CFR Part 40. This is particularly beneficial for regulated industries such as trucking, aviation, pipeline, and transit.
  • Ideal for On-Site and Mobile Testing- Saliva alcohol testing is highly portable, requiring no lab equipment or refrigeration. Accredited Drug Testing offers mobile testing services, allowing for on-site testing at workplaces, schools, events, and moreâ€”helping organizations save time and reduce operational downtime.
  • Affordable and Scalable- Compared to other alcohol testing methods, oral fluid tests are cost-effective and scalable. Whether you\'re testing a single individual or conducting a mass screening, saliva testing is an efficient and budget-friendly solution for employers, treatment centers, and court systems.

Our certified technicians ensure accurate, confidential results for employers, government agencies, and individuals. âœ… Schedule a Saliva Alcohol Test Today â€“ Click Here to Register or call (800) 221-4291.

ETG/ETS Alcohol Testing

ETG (Ethyl Glucuronide) and ETS (Ethyl Sulfate) tests are specialized urine tests that detect alcohol metabolites, not the ethanol itself. These metabolites can remain in the body for up to 80 hours, making ETG/ETS testing one of the most sensitive options for identifying alcohol consumption even after the effects have worn off. This makes it ideal for court-ordered testing, zero-tolerance programs, and addiction recovery monitoring. Accredited Drug Testing offers ETG/ETS testing using SAMHSA-certified labs to ensure legal defensibility and accurate tracking of alcohol use.

Order Your Test Online

ETG alcohol testing is one of the most sensitive and reliable methods for detecting alcohol useâ€”long after ethanol is no longer present in the body. By identifying ethyl glucuronide (ETG), a direct metabolite of ethanol, this testing method offers a longer detection window than standard alcohol tests. ETG testing can be performed using both urine and hair specimens, providing flexible options based on the duration and purpose of testing. At Accredited Drug Testing, we offer ETG alcohol testing services for employers, courts, treatment programs, and individuals nationwide.

Key Benefits of ETG Urine Alcohol Testing

  • Extended Detection â€“ Up to 80 Hours ETG in urine can be detected up to 3.5 days (80 hours) after drinking, depending on the amount of alcohol consumed. This makes it ideal for monitoring abstinence, early recovery, or probation compliance.
  • Cost-Effective and Accessible Urine ETG tests are affordable, easy to administer, and available at thousands of certified locations. Theyâ€™re perfect for frequent testing, such as in outpatient treatment or family court supervision programs.
  • Highly Sensitive ETG urine testing can detect even small amounts of alcohol, including incidental or light drinking. This sensitivity is ideal for zero-tolerance policies, but cutoff levels can be adjusted to minimize false positives from incidental exposure (e.g., mouthwash or hand sanitizer).
  • Accepted in Legal and Clinical Settings ETG urine testing is widely accepted in legal proceedings, rehab centers, DUI programs, and employment monitoring programs where proving abstinence is required

Court Ordered Test Methods

  • Urine Tests: The most common and cost effective method, can detect a wide range of substances for recent use and customized testing methods are available.

    • Benefits of ETG Hair Alcohol Testing

  • 90-Day Detection Window ETG in hair can detect chronic or repeated alcohol consumption over a period of up to 90 days. This is ideal for evaluating long-term drinking patterns, especially in family law, adoption, and immigration cases.
  • Tamper-Resistant and Non-Invasive Hair alcohol testing is virtually impossible to adulterate and can be collected without requiring restroom access or medical personnel. This makes it both secure and convenient for testing in any environment.
  • Ideal for Court and Compliance Programs- ETG hair testing is frequently used in child custody evaluations, pre-employment screenings, professional licensing, and court-ordered monitoring. It provides a long-term view of behavior that breath or urine tests canâ€™t match.
  • Scientifically Valid and Legally Defensible- Results are analyzed by ISO or SAMHSA-certified laboratories, and the testing method is supported by peer-reviewed scientific literatureâ€”making it admissible in court and trusted in regulatory settings.

Whether you need short-term detection or long-term monitoring, we provide confidential, professional, and legally defensible testing for all your alcohol testing needs. âœ… Schedule Your ETG Alcohol Test Today â€“ Click Here to Register or call (800) 221-4291.

Learn More

How Alcohol Metabolizes in the Body and Its Impact on Drug Testing

When you consume an alcoholic beverage, your body immediately begins breaking it down through a process called alcohol metabolism. Understanding this process is critical for interpreting drug and alcohol test results, as different testing methods detect alcohol and its metabolites for varying periods.

Absorption

  • Alcohol is absorbed primarily through the small intestine and stomach lining.
  • It enters the bloodstream within minutes, and peak blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is usually reached within 30-90 minutes after drinking.
  • Factors like food intake, body weight, gender, and drinking speed influence how quickly alcohol is absorbed.

Distribution

  • Once absorbed, alcohol is distributed throughout water-containing tissues in the body.
  • This includes the brain, liver, kidneys, and muscles which explains why alcohol affects both mental and physical functions.

Metabolism

  • About 90 - 98% of alcohol is metabolized in the liver using enzymes, primarily alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH).
  • ADH converts ethanol (alcohol) into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound, before another enzyme, aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), converts it into acetic acid, and eventually into carbon dioxide and water.
  • On average, the liver can process about one standard drink per hour, though this varies per person.

Elimination

    • A small percentage of alcohol (about 2 - 10%) leaves the body unchanged through:
    • Breath Â is Measured by Breath Alcohol Testing (BAT).
    • Urine Â is Detected in urine alcohol testing and ETG/ETS testing.
    • Sweat and saliva used in oral fluid testing..
    • The rest is eliminated after being metabolized in the liver.

Impact of Drug and Alcohol Testing

Because alcohol metabolizes and leaves the system relatively quickly, the detection window depends heavily on the testing method. The bottom Line is, Alcohol\'s rapid metabolism means standard alcohol tests detect only recent consumption, while ETG/ETS and hair tests detect past use by identifying metabolites that remain long after ethanol itself has left the body.

Building a Drug-Free Workplace Culture with Accredited Drug Testing

by John Burgos
on August 14, 2025
Categories: education

Fostering a drug-free workplace isn't just a best practice- it's business imperative. At Accredited Drug Testing, we help employers create and maintain a safe, productive, and compliant work environment through tailored drug testing programs and comprehensive support. Establishing a substance-free culture starts at the top- with clear policies, proactive communication, and reliable testing solutions.

Start with a Clear Policy

A strong drug-free workplace program begins with a clearly written policy that is shared with both new hires and current employees. This policy should outline expectations, testing procedures, and the consequences of violating company drug policies.

It's important that your policy includes:

Pre-employment drug testing

Random drug testing

Reasonable suspicion testing

Post-accident testing

Return-to-duty and follow-up testing protocols

Transparency is key- your team should fully understand that substance use is incompatible with the responsibilities of their role.

Comprehensive Drug-Free Workplace Programs

An effective program includes more than testing:

  • Educational materials and employee training
  • Supervisor training for reasonable suspicion
  • Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) to support recovery
  • DOT-compliant and non-regulated drug testing
  • Policy development and review services

We help employers address emerging challenges like marijuana legalization and prescription drug misuse while maintaining compliance and safety standards.

DOT-Mandated Testing & Industry Compliance

Certain safety sensitive industries are federally required to conduct regular drug and alcohol testing under the Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. This includes:

  • FMCSA
  • FAA
  • FRA
  • FTA
  • PHMSA
  • USCG

Employees in these sectors must undergo pre-employment and random testing, as well as post-accident and reasonable suspicion tests in full compliance with Part 40 Regulations.

Protecting Safety in the Workplace

Workplace safety is one of the most important reasons to implement a drug testing program. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) encourages employers- especially those using heavy equipment or operating in high-risk industries- to maintain drug-free environments.

Employees who are free from substance impairment are more alert, make better decisions, and help prevent costly accidents. Even if your business is not in a safety-sensitive industry, drug testing can still play a vital role in protecting your team and brand.

Testing Options Available at Accredited Drug Testing

We offer a wide range of testing methods at thousands of locations nationwide:

  • Urine Drug Testing
  • Hair Follicle Testing
  • Oral Fluid Testing
  • Breath Alcohol Testing
  • Blood Testing
  • Virtual Drug Testing

Same-day appointments and walk-in options are available.

The High Cost of Substance Abuse in the Workplace

Substance abuse costs U.S. employers over $100 billion annually in lost productivity, absenteeism, injuries, and healthcare costs (U.S. Department of Justice). Commonly misused substances include:

  • Prescription opioids
  • Cocaine
  • Marijuana
  • Methamphetamines
  • Heroin
  • Ecstasy

Implementing a drug testing program is a proactive way to reduce liability, avoid litigation, and safeguard your company from avoidable risks.

Enhance Your Public Image

Your commitment to a drug-free workplace is a powerful brand asset. Clients and customers are more likely to trust companies that uphold safety and professionalism. In competitive markets, a drug-free policy can set you apart from others who have not adopted such standards.

Employer Incentives & Insurance Benefits

Many states offer financial incentives to employers who adopt certified drug-free workplace programs.

These can include:

  • Workers' compensation premium discounts
  • Group health insurance benefits
  • Unemployment claim protection
  • Liability protection following workplace incidents

For example, a positive post-accident drug test may result in denied worker's compensation claims, saving both your company and insurer thousands of dollars.

Partner with Accredited Drug Testing

At Accredited Drug Testing, we provide fast, reliable, and fully compliant drug testing services across the United States. Whether you're regulated by the DOT or simply want to implement a proactive policy, our team of experts- including certified lab technicians and Medical Review Officers (MROs)- is here to support your program every step of the way.


We also offer assistance with drafting and reviewing your company's drug-free workplace policy to ensure it aligns with local, state, and federal guidelines.

College Bound? Preparing Students for Health and Wellness Away From Home

by John Burgos
on August 22, 2025
Categories: education
Heading off to college is an exciting milestone- but it also comes with challenges. For many students, this is their first time living away from home and managing their own health.
At Accredited Drug Testing, we're here to help families prepare for this important transition with practical steps and essential health resources.

The Big Transition

While students may feel eager to embrace independence, the unknowns of college life can bring stress. Parents and guardians can ease that anxiety by making sure their student is fully prepared. A little planning goes a long way toward building confidence and peace of mind.

College Health Must-Haves

Most colleges and universities require students to provide health documentation before move-in.
Here are a few essentials every student should have:

Medication List - Include prescriptions, vitamins, and common over-the-counter medications (such as allergy relief) to avoid dangerous interactions with future prescriptions.
Allergies & Health Conditions - Provide a clear list, along with the names and contact details of primary care and specialty providers.
Emergency Contacts - Beyond parents, list local family, friends, or other trusted adults near campus.
First Aid Kit - Stock with band-aids, pain relievers, hand sanitizer, thermometer, and any special medications specific to the student.
Health Insurance Details - Students should carry their insurance card (or a photo of it saved on their phone) and know how to use it on or off campus.
Immunization Records - Colleges require proof of vaccines, but if you're unsure about your student's immunity, Accredited Drug Testing can help.

The Value of Titer Testing

Immunization records can get misplaced over the years. That's where titer testing comes in. A titer test is a simple blood draw that measures antibodies in the body- confirming immunity to common diseases.

Our Titer Panel checks for immunity to:

Measles - A highly contagious virus affecting the lungs and throat.
Mumps - Spread easily by coughing, sneezing, or sharing drinks and utensils.
Rubella - A viral infection known for its rash and fever.

Titer testing provides peace of mind and ensures compliance with school health requirements.

Supporting Student Wellness Beyond Vaccines

College is often the first time young adults make their own health decisions- including those that affect long-term wellness. Unfortunately, the CDC reports rising cases of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), with over 2.5 million reported cases in the U.S. between 2020 - 2021. 

At Accredited Drug Testing, we provide a judgment-free environment for students who want clarity about their health.

We offer multiple STD Panels that include discreet testing for:

Gonorrhea
Chlamydia
Syphilis
Herpes Simplex Virus I & II
Trichomoniasis

Early detection leads to early treatment- and better outcomes.

Laboratory & Clinical Testing Nationwide

Accredited Drug Testing provides confidential laboratory and blood-analyzed testing services for both medical and personal purposes, including wellness, STD, hormone, allergy, and preventive testing. Patients can schedule same-day testing at any of our 10,000 certified testing centers nationwide- with most locations just minutes from your home, campus, or office.

No doctor visit or insurance required

Physician referral, specimen collection, and full lab analysis included

Confidential and secure result reporting

For students or families with high insurance deductibles, co-pays, or no insurance at all, Accredited Drug Testing offers affordable access to critical wellness testing. Scheduling is fast, easy, and can be done online in just a few steps.

Accredited Drug Testing: Your Partner in Student Health

Whether it's verifying immunizations, getting fast results for common illnesses, or confidential STD testing, Accredited Drug Testing is here to help students and families navigate the college years with confidence.

With over 10,000 testing centers nationwide, we make it simple to get the answers you need. Call today to schedule an appointment and help your student start the school year healthy, prepared, and worry-free.

content:
Accredited Drug Testing welcomes Patrice M. Kelly, JD as Senior Regulatory & Business Consultant

by John Burgos
on August 25, 2025
Categories: education
Orlando, FL - 08/25/2025 - Accredited Drug Testing, Inc. (ADT), the Nation's leading provider of drug, alcohol, and occupational health testing, is proud to announce that Patrice M. Kelly, JD, Co-President of Patrice Kelly Global Solutions, a subsidiary of the Current Consulting Group, has been retained as the company's Senior Regulatory and Business Consultant. In this role, Ms. Kelly will advise the company's President, James A. Greer, and the leadership team on issues including DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements and other federally regulated drug and alcohol testing compliance matters.


"Patrice Kelly's reputation in the drug and alcohol testing industry is unmatched," said James A. Greer, President of Accredited Drug Testing. "Her addition to our team as a consultant ensures that ADT remains at the forefront of compliance, safety, and industry leadership. Our clients will benefit tremendously from her guidance, knowledge, and vision."

Ms. Kelly was the longest-serving Director of the Office of Drug and Alcohol Policy and Compliance (ODAPC) in the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT). For more than three decades, she was the leading trusted advisor to the Secretaries of Transportation, Federal agency leaders, White House personnel, and Congressional staff across multiple Presidential administrations. Recognized as the nation's foremost authority on DOT drug and alcohol regulations, Ms. Kelly has been and continues to be, the expert from whom even other top experts seek advice, both domestically and internationally.

Before joining the Current Consulting Group as the Co-President of Patrice Kelly Global Solutions, Ms. Kelly's career includes historic milestones: she was the first FAA attorney to revoke an air carrier's certificate for failing to implement drug and alcohol testing, initiated the FAA's first civil penalty cases for enforcement of testing regulations, and served as the primary author of DOT's oral fluid testing regulation in 2023. She has written or provided substantive input into nearly every DOT drug and alcohol regulation since 1993. Notably, Ms. Kelly was the only DOT official to have ever served as the decision-maker on Public Interest Exclusions against non-compliant service agents who posed a significant threat to safety. She is a champion for safety who is eager to help clients maintain compliance and shine as the transportation professionals she knows they are.

Her distinguished career spans over 35 years of government service, including senior legal roles with the FAA, special counsel to the Federal Air Surgeon, and a two-year assignment to the National Drug and Alcohol Screening Association (NDASA). She has also worked with the U.S. Supreme Court, the Department of State, and the late Senator Edward "Ted" Kennedy, and began her career on Wall Street.

A graduate of Boston College and member of the Phi Beta Kappa Society, Ms. Kelly earned her Juris Doctor degree from Georgetown University Law Center. She is also a sought-after public speaker and trainer, continuing to champion compliance and safety while supporting the needs of employers, industry partners, and transportation professionals.

About Accredited Drug Testing, Inc.

Accredited Drug Testing, Inc. (ADT) is a nationwide leader in drug, alcohol, DOT regulated services and occupational health testing solutions. Serving thousands of small, medium, and large employers, ADT is known for innovation and expertise. ADT develops cutting-edge programs and services that help employers, individuals, and government agencies maintain compliance while promoting public safety and drug free workplaces. ADT combines advanced technology, streamlined processes, with decades of regulatory knowledge, ADT delivers forward-thinking solutions that set new standards for reliability, efficiency, and customer experience in the drug testing industry.

For more information contact, John Burgos at John@accrediteddrugtesting.com or Sicilia@accrediteddrugtesting.com or call (800)221-4291.

Flu Season and Back-to-School: What Parents Need to Know

by John Burgos
on September 5, 2025
Categories: education

Back-to-School Health: How to Stay Ahead of Flu Season


As a new school year begins, excitement is in the air- new classes, after-school activities, and busy schedules are here once again. But along with all the fun comes a familiar challenge: flu season.


With students spending time in crowded classrooms and sharing close spaces, the chances of catching and spreading the flu go up significantly. At Accredited Drug Testing, we care about keeping families healthy and classrooms thriving. Here's how you can prepare for flu season and help your child stay healthy throughout the school year.


Why Flu Season Hits Schools Hard

Flu season typically peaks between late fall and early spring. Schools, with their high levels of interaction and shared surfaces, make it easy for the influenza virus to spread quickly.

Common flu symptoms include:

  • Fever
  • Cough
  • Sore throat
  • Body aches
  • Fatigue

For students, missing several days of school due to illness can disrupt learning and add stress. That's why prevention and early detection are so important.


4 Ways to Protect Your Family This Flu Season

1. Get the Flu Vaccine

The best way to prevent the flu and its complications is through vaccination.

Schedule your child's flu shot before the season peaks, so they're protected early on.

2. Teach Healthy Habits

Simple habits go a long way in keeping germs at bay. Remind your kids to:

  • Wash hands frequently with soap and water
  • Use hand sanitizer when needed
  • Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or elbow

These small steps can make a big difference in stopping the spread of germs at school.

3. Stay Alert for Symptoms

If your child shows signs of the flu, keep them home from school. Rest, hydration, and early care can help them recover faster while preventing the virus from spreading to classmates.

4. Boost Their Immune System

Help your child stay strong and healthy with:

  • A balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and protein
  • Plenty of sleep
  • Regular physical activity

A healthy lifestyle not only prevents illness but also keeps kids energized for learning and fun activities.

Stay Healthy, Stay Ahead

Flu season doesn't have to mean missed school days and endless tissues. With a few preventive steps and early testing, you can protect your child's health and keep the school year running smoothly.

A 10 panel drug test is one of the most comprehensive drug screening options available. A 10 panel drug test is designed to detect both common and less frequently abused substances. Unlike the standard 5 panel drug test, which primarily screens for marijuana, cocaine, opiates, amphetamines, and PCP, the 10 panel expands coverage to include benzodiazepines, barbiturates, methadone, propoxyphene, and Quaaludes (methaqualone). Employers, courts, and individuals often choose a 10 panel when they need a broader assessment of drug use, making it a trusted option for safety-sensitive industries and legal cases.

Order 10 Panel Drug Test

Key Benefits

  • Comprehensive coverage of 10 major drug classes, including common Rx misuse
  • Multiple specimen options: urine, hair, oral fluid, blood, nails

10 Panel Lab Based Test vs. 10 Panel Instant Test

Understand the differences - speed vs. defensibility - so you can choose the right 10 panel drug test option for employment, court, and personal testing.

At-a-Glance

Both options screen the same 10 drug classes (THC, cocaine, opiates, amphetamines/methamphetamine, PCP, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, methadone, propoxyphene, and Quaaludes*). The difference is how results are produced, verified, and used.

10 Panel Drug Test FAQ\'s

Questions about 10 panel drug testing: Coverage. Detection times, Turnaround, Compliance, and More.

Quick overview: A 10 panel drug test screens for marijuana (THC), cocaine, opiates, amphetamines (incl. methamphetamine), PCP, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, methadone, propoxyphene, and Quaaludes (methaqualone*).

*Available in lab-based testing only

1) What is a 10 panel drug test and which drugs does it detect?

A 10 panel drug test is an expanded screen commonly used for employment, legal, and personal testing. It detects: THC, cocaine, opiates (morphine, codeine, heroin), amphetamines (incl. methamphetamine), PCP, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, methadone, propoxyphene, and Quaaludes (methaqualone*).

2) How long do drugs stay detectable on a 10 panel test?

For urine (most common): many drugs are detectable for ~1â€“3 days; cocaine ~2â€“4 days; PCP ~1â€“7 days; THC up to ~30 days depending on use. Hair testing looks back ~90 days; oral fluid ~24â€“72 hours; nails ~3â€“6 months. Actual windows vary by drug, frequency, metabolism, and lab cutoffs.

3) How fast will I get results and how are they delivered?

Lab-based: negatives typically post ~1 business day after lab receipt; non-negatives usually 2â€“3 business days after confirmatory testing and MRO review. Instant (POCT): screening results in minutes (presumptive) with lab confirmation for non-negatives. Results are delivered securely to the ordering party.

4) Is a 10 panel drug test DOT-compliant?

No. DOT programs follow 49 CFR Part 40 with a specific 5-panel configuration. Order the DOT panel when required. Learn more: DOT Drug Test (5-Panel) Â»

5) What is the difference between lab-based and instant (POCT) 10 panel tests?

Lab-based testing provides defensible results with confirmatory GC/MS or LC-MS/MS and MRO review on non-negatives. Instant tests offer rapid on-site screening; non-negative screens should be lab-confirmed before final decisions. See: 10 Panel Details

6) Will my prescription medications affect the results?

They can. During verification, a Medical Review Officer (MRO) may contact the donor to review valid prescriptions and determine if a non-negative result has a legitimate medical explanation. Always follow the MROâ€™s instructions and provide documentation if requested.

7) Does CBD use cause a positive THC result?

Products labeled â€œCBDâ€ may contain trace THC, especially full-spectrum items, which can trigger a THC positive. THC-free (isolate) products are less likely to cause positives but are not risk-free. Testing policies apply regardless of product source.

8) Can people cheat a 10 panel drug test? How is tampering detected?

Collection sites check temperature and may use adulteration tests and observed collections when required. Labs can detect dilution, substitution, and many adulterants. Tampering can lead to invalid or refused tests per policy.

9) What appears on my lab report and who can see my results?

Reports typically show negative or positive/verified outcomes by drug class; confirmations may include analyte/metabolite details per lab policy. Results are released only to the ordering party and handled confidentially. MRO reviews non-negative lab results.

10) How do I order a 10 panel test and what does it cost?

Order online or by phone and choose a nearby collection site, same-day scheduling is available at over 17,000 locations. Pricing varies by specimen and panel; volume discounts are available for employers. Employment/legal testing is typically not covered by insurance. DOT Physical - What You Need to Know

A DOT physical is a comprehensive medical examination required by the Department of Transportation (DOT) for all commercial motor vehicle (CMV) drivers. This exam ensures that professional drivers are physically, mentally, and emotionally fit to safely operate large vehicles on public roads. The DOT physical is performed by a certified medical examiner (CME) listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners (NRCME). Passing the exam allows drivers to receive a DOT medical certificate (Medical Examinerâ€™s Certificate, also called a DOT medical card), which is required to maintain a valid CDL license under FMCSA regulations. If you are regulated by another DOT agency and need assistance determining which DOT physical is required, call us at 800-221-4291

During your exam, the medical examiner will complete a thorough health assessment to determine if you meet the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) medical standards. The process typically includes:

What Does a DOT Physical Include?

Health History Review
Vision Test

Hearing Test
Urinalysis

Vital Signs
Physical Examination

DOT Testing I DOT Breath Alcohol I DOT Consortium Services I MVR Reports Also Available


What is checked in a DOT Physical?

  • Health history review and medication assessment
  • Vision screening (corrective lenses allowed; minimum standards apply)
  • Hearing assessment (forced whisper or audiometry)
  • Blood pressure and pulse rate
  • Physical examination (systems review)
  • Urinalysis (specific gravity, protein, glucose)

Upon successful completion, your Medical Examiner\'s Certificate (MEC) may be issued for up to 24 months. Some conditions may require shorter certification or specialist documentation

Who needs a DOT Physical?

You must have a valid DOT medical certificate (card) if you:

  • Have a commercial driver\'s license (CDL)- class A,B, or C for interstate commerce
  • Drive a vehicle over 10,001 lbs. GVWR in interstate commerce
  • Transport more than 8 passengers (for hire) or more than 15 passengers (not for hire)
  • Transport hazardous materials that require placarding under DOT regulations
  • Work for employers regulated by DOT agencies such as FMCSA, FAA, FRA, FTA or USCG where DOT medical qualification is required

    • What to bring with you to a DOT Physical?

    • Government-issued photo 
    • Glasses/contacts & prescription
    • List of medications & dosages
    • CPAP usage data (if applicable)
    • Specialist clearances (cardiology, sleep apnea, diabetes, etc.)
    • Recent A1C/blood pressure logs if monitored

    What happens if I fail a DOT Physical?

  • No Medical card will be issued
  • Temporary disqualification
  • Referral for treatment to your primary care doctor
  • FMCSA exemptions for certain medical conditions
  • Employer Notification
  • Next Steps (address the medical issues and retake the exam)

    • .

    What Will Fail a DOT Physical?

    Medical Conditions That Can Fail a DOT Physical

    • Vision & Hearing: Vision worse than 20/40 in each eye (with correction), inability to distinguish traffic signal colors, or hearing loss that prevents hearing a forced whisper at 5 feet.
    • Blood Pressure & Heart Disease: Uncontrolled hypertension (â‰¥180/110 mmHg), recent heart attack, stroke, uncontrolled angina, or an implanted defibrillator without clearance.
    • Diabetes: Uncontrolled diabetes with frequent low blood sugar episodes or complications (neuropathy, vision impairment) that interfere with safe driving.
    • Sleep Apnea & Respiratory Issues: Untreated obstructive sleep apnea causing daytime drowsiness, or severe lung disease impairing oxygenation.
    • Neurological Disorders: Epilepsy/seizure disorders (unless exempted), conditions causing sudden loss of consciousness, dizziness, or uncontrolled tremors.
    • Substance Abuse: Current use of illegal drugs, alcohol dependence, or misuse of prescription medications that impair driving.
    • Psychiatric & Cognitive Disorders: Severe uncontrolled psychiatric illness (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder with recent episodes) or cognitive impairment affecting judgment and reaction time.

    Temporary vs. Permanent Disqualification

    Some issues may only temporarily disqualify you until you provide medical clearance or documentation (e.g., controlled blood pressure, diabetes management). Others, such as untreated seizure disorders or implanted defibrillators, are generally considered permanently disqualifying under FMCSA rules.

Congress Pushes for Broader Marijuana Research Amid Growing Concerns Over Impairment and Public Health

by John Burgos
on September 12, 2025
Categories: education

    A key congressional committee has taken a major step toward expanding marijuana research in the United States. The House Appropriations Committee has approved a spending bill with an attached report calling for studies that better represent 'the variety, quality, and potency of commonly available cannabis strains" that consumers are actually using in today's legal and medical markets.

    For decades, federal marijuana research has relied on a single, federally authorized source, often criticized for not reflecting the potency and diversity of products sold in state-licensed dispensaries across the country. This new direction signals a growing recognition that public health and safety policies require data based on real-world cannabis products, not outdated research material.

Key Points in the Congressional Report

The committee's report, covering Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (LaborH), highlights several pressing concerns:

1. Impaired Driving and Highway Safety

Lawmakers noted the continued lack of an objective standard for marijuana impairment, making it difficult for law enforcement and policymakers to address drug-impaired driving risks. The report encourages the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to:

  • Support research on marijuana's health effects.
  • Investigate how marijuana policies affect public safety.
  • Develop an objective field sobriety test specifically for marijuana impairment.

2. Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome (CHS)

The committee expressed concern about the rising cases of CHS, a condition linked to prolonged, high-potency cannabis use that can lead to severe nausea and vomiting.

With the popularity of high-THC vaping products among adolescents, the report directs the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), and the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) to:

  • Study the prevalence of CHS in youth populations.
  • Investigate correlations between THC vaping and CHS incidence.
  • Deliver an interim report within 180 days and a final report within one year.

3. Limitations on Legalization Advocacy

While calling for expanded research, the LaborH bill also prohibits federal agencies from advocating for the legalization of Schedule I drugs, including marijuana, unless specifically authorized by law or supported by sufficient medical evidence.

What This Means for Employers and Public Safety

As marijuana laws continue to evolve across the U.S., workplace safety and compliance remain critical concerns. Without reliable impairment standards or comprehensive health data, employers face challenges in:

  • Maintaining drug-free workplace programs.
  • Ensuring highway and workplace safety.
  • Responding to new public health risks associated with cannabis use.

Expanded research could pave the way for better testing methods, updated workplace policies, and a clearer understanding of health impacts, ultimately supporting both employers and public health officials in making informed decisions.

What is Labor-H?

Labor-H stands for the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Subcommittee and the annual federal spending bill it oversees.

This bill sets budgets and priorities for key agencies, including:

  • Department of Labor (DOL)
  • Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) - including NIH and CDC
  • Department of Education (ED)
  • Other related agencies such as SAMHSA

Because it covers funding for public health and education programs, the Labor-H bill is where Congress often directs research efforts - such as studies on marijuana impairment, youth vaping, and health effects of cannabis.

  • Nationwide drug testing services for employers, DOT programs, and individuals.
  • Expert compliance guidance on federal and state regulations.
  • Comprehensive training and certification programs for workplace testing and safety.

Alcohol Testing FAQ

by John Burgos
on October 7, 2025
Categories: education
Alcohol Testing Services | DOT & Non-DOT Nationwide

Alcohol Testing Services - Accredited Drug Testing

Accredited Drug Testing provides fast, reliable, and confidential alcohol testing nationwide for DOT-regulated employees, employers, individuals, and legal purposes. Whether you need a breath alcohol test, EtG urine test, or post-accident screening, our certified collection network and federally approved testing methods ensure accurate and compliant results every time.

With thousands of locations across the United States, same-day appointments, and instant testing options available, Accredited Drug Testing makes it easy to stay compliant, protect your workplace, and promote a safe environment for all employees.

Top 15 Alcohol Testing FAQs

1. What is an alcohol test?

An alcohol test measures the presence of ethanol, the intoxicating ingredient in alcohol found in your system using your breath, saliva, urine, or blood. It helps determine if you have recently consumed alcohol and, in some cases, your level of impairment.

2. How is alcohol testing performed?

Alcohol testing can be conducted using a breathalyzer (for instant results), urine tests (to detect recent consumption), blood tests (for precise BAC measurement), oral fluid tests (non-invasive, quick results) or an alcohol hair testing used to detect a pattern of use.

3. What does BAC mean?

BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration, representing the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream. Most states consider 0.08% BAC as the legal limit for operating a vehicle, While Department of Transportation and employers have a much lower level of an acceptable BAC level.

4. How long can alcohol be detected in the body?

Alcohol detection times vary. Breath tests detect alcohol up to 8 hours, urine tests up to 8-12 hours, and EtG/EtS tests may detect alcohol metabolites for up to 80 hours after drinking. While a hair alcohol test can provide a detection window of up to 90-days.

5. What is a DOT alcohol test?

A DOT alcohol test is a federally regulated breath test administered under 49 CFR Part 40 for transportation employees. It must be performed by a certified Breath Alcohol Technician (BAT) using an Evidential Breath Testing device (EBT). Which is conducted by a breath alcohol technician or screening test technician.

6. Who is required to take alcohol tests under DOT rules?

All safety-sensitive employees regulated by the FMCSA, FAA, FRA, PHMSA, and USCG must undergo alcohol testing in specific circumstances including pre-employment, random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, and return-to-duty situations. Check with each agency for specific alcohol testing requirements.

7. What is an EtG alcohol test?

The EtG (Ethyl Glucuronide) test detects alcohol metabolites in urine, providing evidence of drinking for up to 3-4 (80 hours) days after consumption. Itâ€™s often used for court, treatment, and monitoring programs.

8. Can I order an alcohol test for personal reasons?

Yes. Individuals can order confidential alcohol tests through Accredited Drug Testing for personal, legal, or employment purposes. No doctorâ€™s order is required, and same-day appointments are available nationwide. Call us at 800-221-4291 or you can register online.

9. What is the difference between breath and urine alcohol testing?

Breath tests measure current impairment, while urine tests detect alcohol metabolites to determine if alcohol was consumed recentlyâ€”even after itâ€™s left your bloodstream.

10. How fast are alcohol test results available?

Instant breath alcohol test results are available immediately at the testing site. Lab-based test results are typically ready within 24-48 hours from the time the specimen arrives at the lab. Hair and blood testing results may take additional analysis time.

11. Is alcohol testing confidential?

Yes. All alcohol testing conducted through Accredited Drug Testing is completely confidential. Results are securely delivered to authorized recipients only.

12. What happens if an employee tests positive for alcohol?

Under DOT regulations, a positive result (BAC â‰¥ 0.04%) requires immediate removal from safety-sensitive duties and referral to a Substance Abuse Professional (SAP) before returning to work. In a private workplace setting, please refer to your employer's drug free workplace policy.

13. Can medications or mouthwash affect test results?

Some mouthwashes or medications contain small amounts of alcohol that may cause temporary positives. Confirmatory laboratory testing distinguishes between true alcohol use and incidental exposure.

14. What are employer alcohol testing program types?

Employers commonly use pre-employment, random, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and return-to-duty testing programs to maintain safety and compliance.

15. Where can I get an alcohol test near me?

Accredited Drug Testing has over 10,000 locations nationwide. Call 800-221-4291 or order online to schedule your same-day alcohol test.

title: Marijuana and the Modern Workplace: What Employers Need to Know
page_heading: Marijuana and the Modern Workplace: What Employers Need to Know
content:
Marijuana and the Modern Workplace: What Employers Need to Know

by John Burgos
on October 8, 2025
Categories: education

Marijuana legalization is spreading rapidly across the United States, and with it comes a flood of new questions from both employers and employees.

If it's legal in my state, why can't I use it at work?

If marijuana is "natural", doesn't that make it safe?

And if so many states have approved it, why are companies still testing for it?

As laws evolve, workplace safety, federal compliance, and company culture remain at the center of the discussion. Employers must stay informed, proactive, and consistent when developing their drug-free workplace policies.

Legal Confusion: State vs. Federal Law

Public opinion and state laws have changed quickly- far faster than federal regulation. Polls show that roughly two-thirds of Americans support recreational marijuana use, and nearly nine in ten approve of its use for medical purposes under a doctor's care.

Despite these numbers, federal law still classifies marijuana as an illegal Schedule I drug under the Controlled Substances Act.

The 2018 Farm Bill further complicated the issue by removing hemp (and hemp-derived CBD products with less than 0.3% THC) from the definition of marijuana. This change created a booming CBD market but also led to significant public misunderstanding- many people assume all cannabis-related products are legal everywhere, which is not true.

Understanding Safety Risks and Workplace Impact

Whether marijuana is "safe" depends largely on the situation. While many users report therapeutic or relaxing effects, there's growing evidence that it can impair memory, coordination, and reaction time- skills essential to workplace performance.

A Quest Diagnostics Drug Testing Index found a continued rise in marijuana positivity in employee drug tests- up 14% in just three years. States that legalized recreational use, such as Nevada, Massachusetts, and California, saw some of the sharpest increases.

Even more concerning, higher positivity rates have been observed among employees in safety-sensitive roles- where impairment could lead to serious accidents or injuries.

Workplace Safety: An Employer's Responsibility

Employers are legally and ethically responsible for providing a safe environment. Impairment- no matter the source- creates risk.

Recent research shows:

  • 28% admit to using on their way to work, and 22% during lunch breaks.
  • Workplace overdose deaths have risen more than 25% in recent years.

Unlike alcohol, marijuana impairment is difficult to measure in real time. THC metabolites can stay in the body for days or even weeks after use, meaning a positive test doesn't always prove when the substance was used- but it does indicate that it was used, creating a safety and liability concern.

Why Employers Continue to Test

With legalization expanding, some companies are reevaluating their testing policies. But removing marijuana from a drug-testing panel isn't without risk.

Employers in federally regulated industries (such as transportation and aviation) are required to test for marijuana under Department of Transportation (DOT) guidelines. Others may have customer contracts, insurance policies, or federal funding that also require testing.

Even for non-regulated employers, data supports continued testing:

  • Workers who use marijuana have 55% more accidents,
  • 85% more injuries, and
  • 75% higher absenteeism compared to non-users.

One long-term study of postal workers found that employees who tested positive for marijuana had higher rates of absenteeism, turnover, and workplace incidents- even though neither they nor their supervisors knew the results.

Employer Best Practices

If your company is reconsidering its marijuana testing policy, it's important to proceed thoughtfully. Safety and compliance must remain the top priorities.

Employers should:

  • Stay current with state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain clear, updated drug-free workplace policies.
  • Train supervisors to recognize signs of impairment.
  • Educate employees about the effects of marijuana use and how it can impact performance and safety.
  • Use reasonable suspicion and post-accident testing to manage potential risk.

Where Things Stand Now

  • 33 states + Washington, D.C. allow the medical use of marijuana.
  • 10 states permit both medical and recreational use.
  • 14 states allow limited CBD use for medical purposes only.
  • Federal law still prohibits marijuana use or possession nationwide.


In Summary

As marijuana laws continue to evolve, employers must balance public perception with the practical realities of maintaining a safe, compliant, and productive workplace.

Until federal law changes and reliable on-the-job impairment testing becomes available, companies should continue to follow established drug-free workplace policies- protecting both their employees and their business.
